name: prlimit
synopsis: int prlimit(pid_t pid, int resource, const struct rlimit *_Nullable new_limit, struct rlimit *_Nullable old_limit);
description: The prlimit() system call gets and sets resource limits for a specified process. It retrieves the current limits into the old_limit structure and/or sets new limits from the new_limit structure, depending on the arguments provided. Resource limits control aspects like memory size and CPU time for the process.

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description: The process ID of the target process for which limits are to be gotten or set.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: The resource to get or set, such as RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_CPU.

parameters.name: new_limit
parameters.description: Pointer to a new rlimit structure to set the limits, or NULL if not setting limits.

parameters.name: old_limit
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure to store the old limits, or NULL if not retrieving limits.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: A pointer argument points to a location outside the accessible address space.
The value specified in resource is not valid, or for setting limits, rlim->rlim_cur was greater than rlim->rlim_max.
An unprivileged process tried to raise the hard limit.
The caller tried to increase the hard RLIMIT_NOFILE limit above the maximum defined by /proc/sys/fs/nr_open.
The calling process did not have permission to set limits for the process specified by pid.
Could not find a process with the ID specified in pid.

examples: printf("Previous limits: soft=%jd; hard=%jd\n", (intmax_t) old.rlim_cur, (intmax_t) old.rlim_max);
